evidence: The file is declared as domain because its path matches **/core/** (src/modules/authentication/core/application/usecases/register-user/register-user.usecase.ts), but it defines RegisterUserUseCase, which extends UseCase.

RegisterUserUseCase.execute orchestrates identityGateway.checkEmailExists, then passwordHasher.hash, identityGateway.createUser, credentialRepository.save and authorizationGateway.assignDefaultRole. This is a use-case workflow (application kind).

Compensation logic in execute: `await this.credentialRepository.deleteByUserId(registeredUser.id); await this.identityGateway.deleteUser(registeredUser.id);` This is transaction-like coordination that belongs to the application layer.
`import { HttpStatus, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';` brings in HTTP transport and NestJS framework constructs.

`ErrorFactory.UseCaseError('User with this email already exists', null, HttpStatus.CONFLICT)` and the calls using HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR map business failures to HTTP status codes. That is transport (infrastructure/controller) logic.
The `@Injectable()` decorator on RegisterUserUseCase is framework DI wiring and does not belong in a domain file.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit is declared as domain because its path matches **/core/**. But RegisterUserUseCase.execute does application-layer orchestration: it checks the identity gateway, hashes the password, creates the user, saves the credential through the repository, assigns a default role, and undoes earlier steps by hand when a later one fails. This is a use-case workflow across several ports, not a domain responsibility such as an entity, value object or invariant. The file also carries transport and framework concerns. It imports HttpStatus from @nestjs/common and passes HTTP status codes (INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, CONFLICT) to ErrorFactory.UseCaseError, which ties business failure outcomes to HTTP. It also uses the NestJS @Injectable decorator, which is DI framework wiring. HTTP status mapping belongs at the transport boundary, in the infrastructure layer (controllers), whether the file is treated as domain or application. Domain files should hold neither transport nor framework logic. The declared domain layer may be a pattern-precedence misclassification, since the path also contains application/usecases. Even so, the HTTP status coupling would be misplaced in either layer.

execute maps business failures to HTTP status codes (HttpStatus.CONFLICT and HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR from @nestjs/common) in its ErrorFactory.UseCaseError calls. This is transport logic that belongs in the infrastructure layer (controller), not in a domain file.
The @Injectable() decorator from @nestjs/common on RegisterUserUseCase is framework DI wiring. That is an infrastructure/framework concern and does not belong in a domain-layer file.
